title: Local Galactic Structures, Clusters, Remnants & Deep Sky

structures.name: Hyades Cluster
structures.description: The nearest open star cluster to the Solar System, sharing a common trajectory through space.

structures.name: Coma Star Cluster
structures.description: A loose, prominent open cluster located high above the galactic plane in Coma Berenices.

structures.name: Ursa Major Moving Group
structures.description: A co-moving stellar kinematic group containing the core stars of the Big Dipper.

structures.name: Pleiades (Seven Sisters / M45)
structures.description: Luminous young open cluster just beyond the 100-pc boundary, prominent in night-sky lore.

structures.name: Praesepe (Beehive Cluster / M44)
structures.description: One of the nearest open clusters, sharing similar age and proper motion to the Hyades.

structures.name: IC 2602 (Southern Pleiades)
structures.description: Bright young open cluster surrounding Theta Carinae in the southern sky.

structures.name: IC 2391 (Omicron Velorum Cluster)
structures.description: Compact open cluster in Vela visible to the naked eye.

structures.name: Alpha Persei Cluster (Melotte 20)
structures.description: Young OB stellar association surrounding Mirfak in Perseus.

structures.name: Messier 4 (M4 / NGC 6121)
structures.description: The closest globular cluster to the Solar System, situated in Scorpius near Antares.

structures.name: NGC 6397 (Caldwell 86)
structures.description: One of the oldest known globular clusters in the Milky Way with a core-collapsed structure.

structures.name: 47 Tucanae (NGC 104)
structures.description: The second brightest and most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way, located in Tucana.

structures.name: Omega Centauri (NGC 5139)
structures.description: The largest and most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way; remnant nucleus of a dwarf galaxy.

structures.name: Messier 13 (Great Hercules Cluster / M13)
structures.description: The premier northern sky globular cluster in the constellation Hercules; target of the 1974 Arecibo Message.

structures.name: Orion Nebula (M42 / NGC 1976)
structures.description: The closest massive star-forming H II region to Earth, visible to the naked eye in Orion’s Sword.

structures.name: Ring Nebula (M57 / NGC 6720)
structures.description: Iconic bipolar planetary nebula in Lyra ionized by a central white dwarf.

structures.name: Lagoon Nebula (M8 / NGC 6523)
structures.description: Giant interstellar H II emission nebula and star-forming region in Sagittarius.

structures.name: Eagle Nebula (M16 / Pillars of Creation / NGC 6611)
structures.description: Active star-forming H II region in Serpens home to the iconic Pillars of Creation.

structures.name: Carina Nebula (NGC 3372 / Eta Carinae Nebula)
structures.description: One of the largest diffuse emission nebulae in our sky, containing Eta Carinae and the Cosmic Cliffs.

structures.name: Vela Supernova Remnant
structures.description: A massive expanding filamentary remnant of a stellar explosion occurring ~11,000 years ago.

structures.name: Cygnus Loop (Veil Nebula)
structures.description: Spectacular optical emission nebula marking a core-collapse supernova remnant in Cygnus.

structures.name: Crab Nebula (M1 / NGC 1952)
structures.description: Pulsar wind plerion remnant created by the historical supernova of 1054 recorded by Chinese astronomers.

structures.name: Helix Nebula (NGC 7293)
structures.description: The closest planetary nebula to Earth, showing a dying low-mass star shedding its outer gas shell.

structures.name: Dumbbell Nebula (M27 / NGC 6853)
structures.description: The first planetary nebula discovered in history, notable for its bright hourglass morphology in Vulpecula.

structures.name: Local Interstellar Cloud (LIC / Local Fluff)
structures.description: Partially ionised warm interstellar cloud (~7,000 K) in the Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds (CLIC) through which Sol is currently passing.

structures.name: G-Cloud (Galactic Center Cloud)
structures.description: Neighboring warm interstellar cloud (~5,500 K) immediately adjacent to the LIC toward the Galactic Centre, enveloping the Alpha Centauri system.

structures.name: Blue Cloud (Sirius Dog Star Cloud)
structures.description: Compact warm diffuse cloud in the Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds situated along the line of sight to Sirius and Epsilon Canis Majoris.

structures.name: Aquilae Cloud
structures.description: Warm local interstellar cloud in the CLIC extending toward the Aquila and Altair sector.

structures.name: Microscopium Cloud (Mic Cloud)
structures.description: Filamentary warm cloud (~9,900 K) heated by shock interaction at the interface between the Local Interstellar Cloud and the G-Cloud.

structures.name: Leo Cold Cloud (Local Leo Ribbon)
structures.description: Unusually cold (~20 K), dense neutral hydrogen ribbon embedded within the hot Local Bubble cavity at ~7.5 parsecs.

structures.name: Dorado Cloud (Dor Cloud)
structures.description: Southern warm interstellar cloud in the Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds toward Dorado.

structures.name: Eridanus Cloud (Eri Cloud)
structures.description: Warm local interstellar gas cloud in the Eridanus sector of the CLIC.

structures.name: Vela Cloud (CLIC Vela)
structures.description: Fast-moving warm interstellar cloud in the southern Complex of Local Interstellar Clouds.

structures.name: Local Bubble (Local Hot Bubble / LHB)
structures.description: Low-density (~0.001 cm⁻³) interstellar cavity spanning ~200 pc across the Orion Spur, excavated by multiple Pleiades/Sco-Cen supernova explosions over the past 14 million years.

structures.name: Corona Australis Molecular Cloud
structures.description: Compact, high-density molecular cloud complex hosting the young Coronet protostellar cluster at ~130 pc.

structures.name: Rho Ophiuchi Cloud Complex
structures.description: Dense dark nebula and active stellar nursery at the Upper Scorpius boundary of the Local Bubble, ~138 pc from Sol.

structures.name: Taurus Molecular Cloud (TMC-1)
structures.description: The nearest large molecular cloud complex and low-mass star-forming nursery on the rim of the Local Bubble.

structures.name: Pipe Nebula (Barnard 59 / 65–67 / 78)
structures.description: Vast pipe-shaped dark molecular cloud complex in southern Ophiuchus silhouetted against the Galactic Bulge.

structures.name: Lupus Molecular Cloud Complex
structures.description: Chain of star-forming dark molecular clouds (Lupus I–IV) bordering the Scorpius-Centaurus OB association.

structures.name: Coalsack Nebula (Caldwell 99)
structures.description: The most prominent naked-eye dark absorption nebula in the southern Milky Way, silhouetted against Crux.

structures.name: Chamaeleon Cloud Complex
structures.description: High-latitude southern molecular cloud complex rich in T Tauri protostars and reflection nebulae.

structures.name: Sagittarius A* (Galactic Center)
structures.description: Supermassive black hole (4.15 million solar masses) at the dynamical center of the Milky Way galaxy.

structures.name: Geminga (PSR J0633+1746)
structures.description: Radio-quiet gamma-ray pulsar and neutron star created by an ancient local supernova.

structures.name: PSR J0108-1431
structures.description: One of the oldest and closest known isolated radio pulsars to Earth.

structures.name: Vela Pulsar (PSR B0833-45)
structures.description: Rapidly rotating neutron star (period: 89 ms) powering the central filaments of the Vela SNR.

structures.name: Crab Pulsar (PSR B0531+21)
structures.description: Young central neutron star (period: 33 ms) formed in the 1054 CE supernova at the heart of the Crab Nebula.
